toegepas.blok: Wat beeste vir die boere gegee het
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'hulle vleis' can be read as the farmers' own meat; 'die vleis' refers plainly to the cattle's meat.
toegepas.fout: 'hulle' in 'vir hulle vleis' can point to the farmers or the cattle, in a paragraph already full of 'hulle'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'die vleis' removes the ambiguous pronoun without changing who slaughtered what or why.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Afrikaans speaks of a custom 'by' a people or community; 'van' reads woodenly here.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'n gebruik van gemeenskappe' is natural Afrikaans; 'by' only reads differently, so this is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'nie seker weet nie' is colloquial; 'nie seker wees of ... nie' is the standard idiom and keeps the same meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Ons weet nie seker of ... nie' is plain, natural Afrikaans for a Grade 5 reader; the proposal is merely different.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Wat beeste vir die boere gegee het
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: beeste aangehou wat hulle op baie maniere gehelp het
laat_vaar_vorige.na: beeste aangehou, en die beeste het hulle op baie maniere gehelp
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: With 'wat hulle' a young reader can briefly take 'wat' as object (the farmers helped the cattle); naming the subject removes the ambiguity, and the AWS comma is required between the two clauses.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The heading and the paragraph make 'the cattle helped the farmers' the only sensible reading, and the proposal adds a clumsy repeat of 'beeste' in a paragraph already full of it.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Ons sê so 'n gesin het hoë status gehad
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Ons sê dat so 'n gesin hoë status gehad het
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Written study text reads better with the full 'dat' clause and verb-final order than with the spoken form without 'dat'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Leaving out 'dat' after 'sê' is normal, natural Afrikaans, so this is a sideways change rather than a fix.
